_about: Lexical-lane harness fixtures (v4.21, 2026-09-10). Same fictional workshop
world as fixtures.json (Anvil the laptop, Bellows the workstation, Quill the
coding agent) — a separate file so the E2 gates keep their frozen world.
Every memory carries an IDENTIFIER: an advisory id, an error string, a
commit hash, a file name, a port, a CVE. Every query names one identifier
and little else — the case the lexical lane exists for. Decoys share the
topic (three advisories, two commits, two ports, two CVEs) so meaning alone
cannot pick the answer; only the words can.
PADDING: 61 look-alike decoys (pad-*) with different identifiers, so the store
outgrows the kNN pool (overfetch 15 for max_results 5) the way a real tenant does
— with 14 memories the pool held the whole store and the lane could only re-order.
Vectors: the production embedder (nomic via Ollama), cached in
embeddings.json by tests/recall/embed_fixtures.py like the E2 world.
gate: measured floors, never tuned to pass — recorded from the first honest
run with the lane ON. control: the SAME queries with the lane OFF must score
below the gate, or the lane is not doing anything on this world.
Every id, hash, path, host and number here is invented.
First honest run (2026-09-10, w_lexical 0.10, 75 memories / 11 queries):
lane ON recall@5 1.000, MRR 1.000, top-1 100%; lane OFF (control) recall@5
1.000, MRR 0.848, top-1 73% — three identifiers lost rank 1 to a look-alike.
Floors = baseline minus one whole query over 11 (1/11 = 0.0909): 0.909 / 0.909.

memories.summary: Advisory GHSA-7q2x-4mvp-9rrk in the csv reader was accepted: the import tool calls parse() with no options, so the vulnerable branch is unreachable.
Advisory GHSA-3h8k-p2wc-5nnt in the stream json parser was accepted: local-only tooling, not a running server; waiting on upstream.
Advisory GHSA-9vd4-j6r7-2mmx in the xml parser rides the upstream lockfile gate: dev-only chain, not installed in the live deploy.
The seal step on Bellows died with httpx.ReadTimeout after 120 s while the server finished the tenant behind it; rerun verify before sealing again.
The bridge on Anvil logged ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:50001 for six minutes after the reboot; the path was wrong, not the service.
Commit 4b1d9e2 broke ledger seal --all on archived tenant directories; the fix landed as 379f571.
Commit 7f8a801 removed the read cap on the seal POST so a slow tenant no longer kills the whole run.
A crash fragment at the tail of ledger.jsonl is quarantined to ledger.torn so one crash never bricks adoption.
The fleet key vault lives on at ~/.lever/keys.json even though the Lever service itself was retired.
The bus listener on Bellows is port 9137, restarted by a logon task with a hidden window.
Quill's dashboard is port 3001 on Anvil, reachable on the tailnet behind a login gate.
CVE-2031-40412 is a V8 out-of-bounds write; browser build 153.0.8010.36 carries the fix on both machines.
CVE-2031-38820 was the earlier V8 bug; the snap build never got a fix and was retired for the vendor build.
The reasoning model on Bellows is qwen2.5:32b-instruct on the local runner; the embedder is nomic-embed-text.
